title: "Tutorials"
description: "Hands-on guides and courses for lab tools and analysis workflows."
---

Step-by-step guides for the tools and analysis workflows used in the lab,
grouped into tracks. Some tutorials live here in the wiki; others are
maintained as separate sites and linked below.

New to the lab? Work through [Foundations](#foundations) in order, then pick up
the other tracks as your project needs them.

## Foundations

Core skills every lab member needs. These are self-paced
[Software Carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org/) lessons.

1. **[The Unix Shell](https://swcarpentry.github.io/shell-novice/)** —
   navigating files and running programs from the command line. You'll need it
   for Git, the lab servers, and the cluster.
2. **[Git and GitHub](git-github.qmd)** — tracking changes to your work and
   contributing to lab repos. Follows the Software Carpentry Git lesson and ends
   with your first pull request to this wiki.
3. **A programming language** — do the one your project uses; ask your mentor
   if you're not sure.
   - [Programming with Python](https://swcarpentry.github.io/python-novice-inflammation/)
   - [Programming with R](https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-inflammation/)

## Lab workflow

How we build and share research code and data. Start these once you're
comfortable with Foundations.

- **[FAIR data and software](https://librarycarpentry.github.io/lc-fair-research/)** —
  principles for making data and code findable, accessible, interoperable, and
  reusable. A Library Carpentry lesson that is still in pre-alpha, so expect
  rough edges.
- **[Spec-driven development with coding agents](https://www.deeplearning.ai/courses/spec-driven-development-with-coding-agents)** —
  a DeepLearning.AI course on writing clear specs that give a coding agent the
  context it needs to build maintainable software. Take it after Git and a
  programming language: you need to be able to read and check the code an
  agent writes.

## Analysis

- **[Single-cell analysis tutorials](https://omnia-lab-uc.github.io/single-cell_tutorials/)** —
  a hands-on course for single-cell analysis in R using data from the Seattle
  Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD). Runs from environment setup
  through reading and inspecting `.h5ad` files. Aimed at students and anyone new
  to single-cell work; assumes a working R/RStudio and Quarto setup. Maintained
  in the [`single-cell_tutorials`](https://github.com/Omnia-Lab-UC/single-cell_tutorials)
  repo.
